data.exact_reserve_text: The 2021 underwriting year has been impacted by a number of climate related natural catastrophes such as Hurricanes Ida and Ian, Storms Uri and Elliot, various flooding catastrophes and the Volker hail event. The war in Ukraine has also impacted the 2021 underwriting year. Despite this challenging claims environment the syndicate is expected to produce a positive return on capacity for 2021 underwriting year - indicating that such events are within the syndicate's expected range.

data.standardized_narrative: Gross claims outstanding increased from 4,981.9 to 5,878.4 (USD millions) during 2022. The syndicate notes that the 2021 underwriting year was impacted by several climate-related natural catastrophes (Hurricanes Ida and Ian, Storms Uri and Elliot, various floods and the Volker hail event) and geopolitical shock (war in Ukraine). Despite these pressures and macroeconomic headwinds (inflation and rising interest rates) the managing agent expects a positive return on the 2021 underwriting year. The report does not disclose a single explicit gross prioryear development (PYD) figure for reserve movements; no gross PYD amount could be extracted from the disclosed notes.

data.data_quality_notes: No explicit gross prior-year development (PYD) figure for claims outstanding was found in the provided notes. The technical reserves reconciliation shows total movement in gross claims outstanding for the year but this includes current-year development and therefore was not used per instructions. As a result prior_year_development_gbp_m is null. Exact reserve-movement text describing PYD is not provided; narrative referencing the 2021 underwriting year impact and expected positive return was used. LOB movements by reserve are not disclosed; lob_movements entries are therefore left with null amounts. All monetary figures are reported in the report's functional currency (USD) and are expressed in millions.
